Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Five riders currently ask for a regular trip, and two more call the coordinator when they receive an appointment letter.

Tuesday clinic departures are usually from Juniper Court at 8:20 a.m. and Larch House at 8:35 a.m. The clinic asks patients to arrive fifteen minutes before appointments. Asha Malik normally drives the Tuesday route and can take three passengers besides herself. She has covered six of the past eight Tuesdays. Her note on the rota says, “I can keep doing Tuesdays through October, but I need the second Tuesday off for my own appointment.” On the other two recent Tuesdays, Leon Price drove one trip and the trip was cancelled once because nobody had confirmed a driver by Monday afternoon. The rider who missed that trip was later offered a Thursday slot, but the notes do not say whether that worked for them.

Thursday clinic trips have less settled times. The two regular riders have appointments between 10:00 a.m. and 1:30 p.m., and the clinic sometimes changes appointment times with only a few days’ notice. Mei Ortiz has driven four Thursdays recently, usually collecting both riders, while Tom Adeyemi covered one Thursday when Mei was away. Mei’s car has room for two passengers and a folding walker, but not a wheelchair. Tom can take one passenger and has asked for two days’ notice because he shares his car with his partner. The remaining Thursday entry on the paper rota says “ask around”; no driver was recorded. Nia said, “We should not promise a ride until someone has actually said yes.”

The Friday grocery run leaves Juniper Court at 11:00 a.m. and Larch House at 11:15 a.m. The driver waits at the market for up to 45 minutes, then brings riders home. Ruth Ivers has driven three of the last four Fridays. Her car fits two passengers and their shopping bags, although she cannot lift heavy bags into the trunk. The fourth run was covered by Samir Cole, who can drive only on the first and third Friday of each month because of a daytime work shift. One resident has asked whether the van could stop at the pharmacy on the way back. Nobody has checked with the other riders, and the notes do not establish whether the van is allowed to make an additional stop.

Mei is unavailable on the last Thursday of each month. Tom has not confirmed any dates beyond the end of September. Ruth said she will be away from October 18 through October 25. Samir’s first-Friday availability in October has not been confirmed. The contact sheet lists two possible backup drivers, Bea Lang and Curtis Wynn, but neither has driven for this rota yet; Nia has not checked whether their cars can accommodate the regular riders’ mobility aids. No one has recorded a current vehicle inspection date for Leon’s car.

A short safety discussion at the library on September 12 produced three comments. Bea asked whether volunteers should wait inside the building if a rider is late; the group did not settle that question. Curtis said, “I can help with calls, but I’m not ready to drive people I haven’t met.” Ruth reported that one passenger had been waiting outside in rain because the driver had used the side entrance rather than the main doors. The passenger’s name and trip date were not written down. Nia said she would add a reminder about the main entrance to the rota, but it is unclear whether she has done so. The current paper sheet has no space for recording a rider’s preferred contact method or mobility equipment.

1. On September 19, Asha confirmed that she can drive the first and third Tuesdays in October, but she has not committed to later Tuesdays. Leon said he might cover the second Tuesday if his car inspection is current; nobody has checked the inspection date. Nia has not contacted Bea or Curtis about those dates.
2. On September 21, Mei said she expects to be available for the first two Thursdays in October, subject to appointment changes. Tom could cover October 24 if asked by October 22, but he has not agreed to that trip. The clinic has not yet supplied November appointment times. One regular rider uses a folding walker; the other’s mobility needs are not described in the notes.
3. Ruth confirmed she is available for the first two Fridays in October and away from October 18 through October 25. Samir is available October 4 but has not confirmed October 18. The rota shows a grocery run on October 11, but no driver is written beside it. The resident who asked about a pharmacy stop has not said which pharmacy or whether the request is urgent.
4. Nia has a draft contact sheet with spaces for a driver’s name, date, pickup times, and rider count. She has not added fields for vehicle capacity, mobility equipment, preferred contact method, or a backup driver. The library can print a revised sheet, but the person who normally handles printing is away until October 7.
5. The town has announced that River Road will be closed for drainage work from October 14 through October 20 if heavy rain delays the first phase. The notice says the closure is conditional on that delay; no updated start date has been issued. River Road is the usual route between Larch House and the clinic. The detour adds about twelve minutes in normal traffic, but volunteers have not tested it during the morning rush.

At the September 26 rota check-in, Nia asked each driver to report changes directly to her rather than editing the library copy without notice. Leon said he could help maintain the paper sheet but is not sure he can reliably check messages during his workday. Mei offered to make a temporary call list for October, while Ruth asked that riders be told about any pickup-time change before the day of travel. No one has agreed on who will contact riders if a driver cancels after confirming.
